newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA RELIES ON FOREIGN LOANS TO REPAY DEBT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA RELIES ON FOREIGN LOANS TO REPAY DEBT.

text.p: Bulgaria relies entirely on external loans to repay pending foreign debt of nearly one billion dollars due this year, Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriisky said on Thursday.

"Without financial support from the European Union and international lending institutions we will not be able to service our obligations to these organisations due this year," Gavriiski told reporters.

Speaking after the first session of the new interim cabinet, he said he hoped that some $200 million dues to the EU and $126 million to the Paris Club of official creditors could be repaid only by new EU loans.
"We hope to receive between $300 million and $400 million from the EU," said Gavriiski.

Missions are expected in the next few days from the European Union, and from the International Monetary Fund, which suspended credits last year because of the Socialists' failure to carry out promised reforms.

Coupon payments on Brady bonds issued two years ago to restructure an $8.16 billion commercial debt due in July should not be a problem if Bulgaria received funding for its other debts, said Gavriiski.

The cabinet, led by Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski, inherits economic chaos from the outgoing Socialist administration. Bulgaria has been without effective government since Zhan Videnov resigned as premier and party leader on December 21.

The cabinet also set up a Financial Stabilisation Council headed by Sofianski and including Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriisky, central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov, Chavdar Kanchev, director of Bulgarian foreign trade bank Bulbank, and former debt negotiator Ventsislav Antonov.
The council will implement financial stabilisation policy and negotiate with international lenders. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
